title: Incremental guarded adoption controller for Optimize suggestions with synthetic canary injection
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Implement a guarded adoption controller that can safely auto-apply Optimize recommendations (batching and KV/cache presets) by running progressive, observable canaries and enforced rollback conditions. This ticket scopes the controller, a synthetic-canary generator that replays anonymized production traces against candidate configs, and an approval matrix for human-in-loop escalation. The controller should be pluggable into the existing rollout pipeline, emit detailed observability events, and support dry-run simulation mode before any live commit. Goal: reduce manual application time while keeping application-level SLO regressions below the defined safety budget.
acceptance_criteria: Controller runs a staged adoption sequence: dry-run -> synthetic-canary -> 1% live -> 10% live -> 100% live with automatic rollback triggers
Synthetic canary runner replays production-like traces with adjustable traffic skews and reports cost/latency/quality deltas

Rollback occurs automatically when any configured safety signal crosses threshold (latency p95, error rate, quality regression on eval set, cache hit drop) and a revert is recorded as an auditable operation
Approval matrix respects team-level gates: infra, platform, and product owners must be able to require manual approval at any stage
Console surfaces canary metrics, safety budget consumption, and a one-click manual rollback path
All changes have associated traceable artifacts: simulation outputs, canary payloads, and transient logs stored for 30 days
implementation_notes: Create a controller service that accepts candidate Optimize configs and orchestrates phases: simulate, synthetic_canary, live_ramp, finalize
Synthetic canary subsystem will use sampled, anonymized request traces from the Replay Store; implement throttling to avoid overloading model endpoints during replay

Define safety signals and thresholds in a policy document; signals include p95 latency, p99 latency, error rate, generation quality delta (based on eval harness), embedding distance regressions, and cache hit ratio
Integrate with existing rollout-event bus for auditability and with Console for visualization; emit structured events for each phase
Design the controller to support compensation actions: immediate revert, half-step throttle (reduce target traffic percent), forcibly warm KV cache, or switch to compatible model variant
Expose a dry-run API that returns simulated metrics and a human-readable risk summary to be attached to approval requests
Add unit and e2e tests that mock the replay store and validate rollback logic under injected failure modes
